title: Event Hydrator: correlate producer identity and map service fields for structured log ingestion
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current log ingestion receives heterogeneous JSON shapes from multiple producers (host agents, application libs, gateway) and inconsistent correlation propagation (traceparent/x-correlation-id missing or under different keys). This causes gaps in trace->log joins, label sparsity in Loki, and inconsistent ES mappings that break Kibana dashboards.

Goal: Build an "Event Hydrator" service (stateless, horizontally scalable) that normalizes incoming structured logs, preserves/proxies correlation identifiers, maps producer metadata to canonical service fields, validates schemas, and emits a single enriched kafka topic for downstream consumers (Loki/ELK). The hydrator should operate behind a feature-flagged ingest path and support a shim for legacy producers.

Design highlights:
- Ingest path: producers -> ingest-gateway -> event-hydrator -> kafka log-enriched.v1 -> downstream consumers (loki-ingest, elastic-ingest).
- Correlation propagation: hydrate traceparent/x-correlation-id into top-level "correlation.id" and add secondary fields trace_id/span_id when present. If missing, optionally synthesize a UUID and mark as synthetic.
- Producer identity: canonicalize service_name, host.host_id, tenant_id. Accept a mapping table (S3/ConfigMap) to translate known producer IDs to canonical names for indexing.
- Schema mapping: validate against a thin schema registry (jsonschema per message-type). Drop invalid messages to dead-letter topic with reason metadata; count and alert on DLQ growth.
- Loki labels: extract stable label set (tenant, service_name, environment) and keep unstructured payload in message field to minimize cardinality in Loki. For Elastic, ensure consistent field types and nested structures for observability dashboards.
- Performance & reliability: continuous batching with max latency 20ms for hot path, backpressure via HTTP 503 + Retry-After when Kafka partition lag > threshold, circuit-breaker to prevent cascading failures.
- Observability: expose prometheus metrics (ingest_in, enriched_out, dlq_count, enrichment_latency_ms_histogram, synth_correlation_count), traces (using existing tracing hooks), and structured self-logging.

Migration plan:
1) Deploy hydrator to staging; replay a week of production traffic (in-place) to compare outputs.
2) Enable feature-flagged path for 1% production traffic; monitor metrics and dashboards (ingest latency, 5xx, DLQ).
3) Incremental canary (5%, 25%, 100%) with rollback playbook.
4) Once stable, flip producers to direct output to hydrator and deprecate old shims.

Notes: Keep hydrator schema changes additive. Any field renames must pass through a compatibility transformer to avoid breaking linked dashboards and monitors.
acceptance_criteria: Event Hydrator service deployed to staging and reads from the ingest-gateway test topic
Hydrator emits to kafka topic 'log-enriched.v1' with expected canonical fields
Correlation id preserved or synthesized and present in >99.9% of enriched messages
No increase in 5xx error rate or 99th percentile ingest latency during 1% canary
DLQ exists and messages include schema validation failure reason; DLQ growth triggers alert
Updated Loki and Kibana dashboards show logs joined to traces via correlation.id for sampled requests
Runbook for rollback and mitigation published and referenced in attachments
comments: 2025-02-18 Maya Chen: Initial triage — sketched architecture and trade-offs. Decided against per-producer adapters; prefer a single hydrator with a mapping table to simplify deployments.

2025-02-25 Arjun Patel: Architecture review completed with infra and platform SREs. Agreed on kafka topic contract and DLQ behaviour. SRE requested backpressure semantics and a hard cap on concurrent transform routines.
2025-02-28 Design feedback (June Park): Please ensure Loki label set is minimal to avoid high cardinality (tenant, service_name, env only). Add 'synthesized' flag when correlation id is injected.
2025-03-01 QA (Luca Morales): Staging replay ran for 3 hours. Found edge cases where nested 'request.id' was an array; updated schema to coerce to string and put original path into metadata.
2025-03-03 Arjun Patel: PR opened for hydrator service + helm chart (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821). Integration tests added for correlation propagation and DLQ routing.

2025-03-04 SRE (Priya Nair): Canary schedule proposed: 2025-03-10 start at 1% for 4 hours, then 5% for 6 hours, then 25% for 24 hours. Add dashboard alerts for enrich_latency_p95 > 150ms and dlq_rate > 0.5%.
2025-03-04 Arjun Patel: Noted an intermittent producer where service_name is sent as numeric id; added mapping rule and will seed mapping table with known legacy ids before canary.
